evidence.finding: Candidate side (Op Name batch_norm_with_update_kernel, Block Dim 64, Task Duration 81.46us): per-block aiv_time mean 39.70us, of which aiv_vec_time 15.37us (ratio 0.388), aiv_mte2_time 14.68us (0.370), aiv_mte3_time 4.89us (0.123), aiv_scalar_time 10.69us (0.268); aiv_scalar_mte2_stall_time 8.86us. Per block MTE2 instructions 165, MTE3 37, read_main_memory 256KB, write_main_memory 128.5KB. Pipe time sums to ~1.15x the per-block wall, so MTE2 and VECTOR are almost additive rather than overlapped, and neither pipe is saturated (both <40%).

Partial common-clock window (absolute_time_qualified=false, timeline_qualified=false): VECTOR productive_ratio 0.4919, wait_only_ratio 0.3089, idle_ratio 0.1991; SCALAR productive 0.0748, wait_only 0.5790, idle 0.3462; MTE2 productive 0.3114, idle 0.6886, wait_only 0.0; MTE3 has no timeline lane. Regions attribute repeated instruction time to the stats loop lines 51-66, with WAIT_FLAG/BAR entries mapped to lines 53/57 and largest single-instruction time 6.64us. Distinguishes 'tile load latency not hidden' from 'vector compute saturation': a large explicit-wait share coexists with low idle on VECTOR, i.e. the vector core is mostly waiting inside the loop rather than being compute-bound. These are fractions of a partial window, not device time and not proof of a dependency.

Both phases are plain nested scf.for loops over 8x128 fp32 tiles: each iteration performs a single tt.load of the current tile, then the dependent Welford delta recurrence on that loaded value, and the second loop does load -> arith -> tt.store. There is no lookahead/second load in flight, so the load of iteration k+1 cannot be issued before the compute of iteration k; the 8x128 tile is eight strided 512B rows per load.
Retained source dbf93822 evaluation: geo_mean 1.2923, timing-7 (8x64x64x64 fp32) 71.55us vs CANN 28.39us (0.397x), timing-8 71.81us, fp16/bf16 8x64 cases ~64-67us, all 27 formal cases PASSED.

hypothesis: Each program (one per feature, 64 programs on the target case) executes a serial chain of 32 stats tiles plus 32 normalize tiles; every tile load is consumed immediately by the dependent Welford/normalize math, so the full GM load latency of each iteration is exposed and MTE2 cannot overlap VECTOR. With 24MB total traffic and MTE2 active bandwidth only ~16.6GB/s per core, the kernel is not bandwidth-bound and not vector-throughput-bound; it is bound by un-overlapped per-iteration load-use latency (~0.62us/iteration x 64 iterations ~= 39.7us per block).
change: Software-prefetch one tile ahead in both kernel loops: keep a current tile and issue the load for n_step+1 into a next tile before the Welford update / normalization of the current tile, then rotate. Same BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N heuristics, same mask construction, same delta-form Welford and same second-pass formula; only the load scheduling changes.
expected: Per-block aiv_time 39.7us -> roughly 28-32us; kernel wall (profiled 81.5us, timed 71.5us for timing-7) -> about 52-62us; MTE2 and VECTOR active overlap increases while read/write byte counts and instruction counts stay essentially unchanged; numeric output identical (same values and recurrence per lane), so all 27 formal cases remain PASSED.
validation: Bridge preflight --source candidate.py for compile/route review, then host-run formal 27-case evaluation plus 36 supplementary checks; if qualified, re-collect paired profiling and simulator evidence for this new source SHA and compare per-block aiv_time, MTE2/VECTOR ratios and byte counts against dbf93822.
alternatives: Reduce iteration count with a larger tile (fewer, larger DMA transfers): would cut round-trip count but leaves the load-use dependency and raises UB pressure.
Set num_stages=2 in the triton.Config so the backend pipeliner multi-buffers the loop: depends on backend support for non-dot loops and may be a no-op.
Split the reduction across more programs with a second kernel/atomics: adds a launch and cross-block reduction, changes summation grouping, and is not justified while per-block latency dominates.
Replace Welford with plain sum/sum-of-squares to shorten the vector chain: numerically riskier on fp32 large-value cases and the vector pipe is not the saturated resource.
discriminating_observation: Issue the next tile's GM load before computing the current tile (double buffering) while keeping tile shapes, masks, traffic (256KB read + 128.5KB write per block) and the Welford recurrence order per lane identical. If load-use serialization is the limiter, per-block aiv_time should fall and MTE2 busy time should overlap VECTOR busy time (both active ratios rise) with unchanged instruction/byte counts. If per-block time and the MTE2/VECTOR ratios stay put, the loop dependency is not the limiter and the larger-tile or sumsq explanations must be tested instead.
